title: Give the planner a mechanical caller list and exit table for changed
summary: Root cause: the planner is told in prose to list every caller and mode (jobs 20261030-013555-f5qm, 20261031-030119-tw3v, 20261103-075205-wbtm), but its brief never shows it the callers of the functions in the deliverable files, and it has no rule to tabulate each exit of a changed stage. Fix in the planner brief inputs (information, not a refusal): Athena computes the callers of each existing Rust deliverable's functions from the base snapshot and puts them in the brief with a new exits rule.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the brief text a planner receives, not only that the code exists.
New unit tests in athena-context and athena-core; the verifier runs cargo test for the two crates.
The fix is in the planner's inputs and brief, not in a per-job workaround.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs (planner_brief, OPEN_QUESTION_RULE, CODE_CLAIMS_RULE, FIELD_MEANING_RULE, DeliverableFact), crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs tests around lines 1800-1850 and 4169-4212, and crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs lines 95-155, where the planner brief is built and deliverable facts come from git.show_file. The entry point is planning_round, which calls planner_brief. No record or data file is added, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are not touched. The property is measured directly by asserting the rendered brief text.

Prior jobs: 20261030-013555-f5qm, 20261031-030119-tw3v and 20261103-075205-wbtm each stopped at round 3 with code-answerable findings (the max_concurrency path, record loss on drop, role limits). Their candidates changed no files, so there is nothing to keep or drop. Each finding is addressed as a class: the brief now carries the callers and exits that the missing information concerned. Their own deliverables (drain.rs, landing.rs, xtask site.rs and similar) are out of scope here and need separate retries.

The prose rules landed earlier (OPEN_QUESTION_RULE, CODE_CLAIMS_RULE) and the admission check on open questions already cover part of the class. The remaining gap is the computed facts and the exit table, which the latest introspection (job 20261115-202532-6mng) names.

Callers are found by textual search of the base snapshot (fn name followed by an opening parenthesis), capped per function. This is approximate, and the brief labels it as a starting list the planner must extend, not a complete one.
Goal and audience: the planner and critic roles are the audience; fewer plans stop at the round cap on findings that reading code would settle.
Existing code: crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs are extended, not replaced.
Environment: no CI workflow, push or records read; the work is local to the snapshot and tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change description names the root cause: the planner brief gives no computed list of existing callers or exits for the functions in the deliverable files, only prose, so plans skipped adjacent paths such as `[parallel] max_concurrency` into landing. Checked in the diff of CHANGELOG.md and the doc comment on the new code in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs.

DeliverableFact in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs gains a callers field. A unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs builds a planner brief and asserts that each caller (file:line) appears in the deliverables section. Run: cargo test -p athena-context.

A test in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs or run/tests.rs computes callers from a fixture snapshot where a function in a deliverable file has callers in two other files. It asserts both are listed, and that a deliverable with no callers is shown as such, not omitted. It fails without the change. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A new exits rule const in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs is added to the planner Report. It requires a plan that changes a stage or core flow to tabulate every exit (success, fail, error, hold, interrupt) with the file:line that handles it. A test in briefs.rs asserts that wording appears exactly once, in a first-round brief and in a revision brief.
No refusal rule is added. admission.rs and the reading checks are unchanged, so expected 0% of newly refused readings.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change.

out_of_scope: Any new refusal rule or change to crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs
Retrying the content of jobs 20261030-013555-f5qm, 20261031-030119-tw3v and 20261103-075205-wbtm (the landing queue, send_back, owner briefs)
Changes to prompt .md files, which have almost no token headroom
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass rate than the reference: the change spans two crates and the caller search over the snapshot is new code.
urgent_reason: It cuts planning rounds that fail at the round cap on findings that reading code would settle, which wastes retries.
hard_reason: This changes the run pipeline: how the planner is briefed and how planning inputs are built.
